text: Every grid keeps a list. It is called critical load, and it is the set of customers who do not get shed no matter what.
provenance: It is called critical load, and it is the set of customers who do not get shed no matter what: hospitals, water plants, emergency services, and the infrastructure the grid itself depends on.

text: The obvious answers are on it. Hospitals. Water treatment. Emergency dispatch.
provenance: The obvious answers are on it.

text: Most natural gas production and processing facilities in Texas were not identified as critical load.

text: So when the operator shed twenty thousand megawatts to save the grid, some of what went dark was the gas industry that fuelled it.

text: Compressor stations stopped. Processing plants stopped. Wells that needed power stopped. Which took fuel sources offline. Which forced further load shedding.
The grid cut power to save itself, the power it cut fed the fuel system, the fuel system stopped, and the grid had to cut more.

text: Nobody in that chain did anything wrong at the moment they did it. That is what makes it a loop and not a mistake.
